newsitem.title: USA: Food Lion agrees to tape comments for ABC.
newsitem.headline: Food Lion agrees to tape comments for ABC.

text.p: Food Lion Inc said Friday it had "reluctantly" agreed to tape two minutes of comments concerning its imbroglio with ABC Television's "PrimeTime Live" newsmagazine show.
Its tape will be shown in a planned 60-minute report by PrimeTime to be broadcast February 12, Food Lion said.

In January, ABC lost a civil complaint by the supermarket chain, which sued the television network over a 1992 PrimeTime undercover report alleging the company sold spoiled meat and outdated goods and did not use sanitary food handling practices.
A jury found ABC committed fraud, trespass and breach of loyalty and recommended that the network, which is a unit of Walt Disney Co, pay $5.5 million in damages to Food Lion.

ABC had previously announced that it wants the jurors for the February 12 airing of PrimeTime Live to focus on investigative journalism, saying its case with Food Lion had opened public debate about the role of the media and the relationship of the press to the public.

In a letter to the show's executive producer, Food Lion spokesman Chris Ahearn said, "While we hesitate to participate in PrimeTime Live's shameless and thinly veiled attempt to retry the case ABC already has lost in court, we feel it will be the only opportunity for Food Lion to present its point of view."

He called ABC's offer to air Food Lion's side "an invitation to a minefield," noting it will only have two minutes out of 60 minutes and that the topics to be debated and the parties in the debate are unknown to it.
An ABC spokeswoman for PrimeTime Live was not immediately available to comment.
Food Lion is a unit of Belgian retailer Ets Delhaize Freres et cie "Le Lion" SA.
